Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) I attached a short SOW and the proposed evaluation playbook for the three-region performance run (US / EU / APAC). High level:

- Objective: Validate TTFT, latency (p50/p95), sustained throughput and concurrency envelope for your core inference workload and measure multi-region routing + failover impact.
- Scope: 3 synthetic traffic profiles (chat-heavy, code-completion, embedding batch) that mirror your production token distribution.

- Environment: Dedicated test reservation in our US region; EU and APAC scheduled as parallel runs. We’ll use the same model family and quantization profile you requested (llama-equivalent q4_0).
- Timeline: Kickoff April 13 — data ingest and baseline tests April 14–15 — high-concurrency runs April 16–17 — failover routing sweep April 18 — synthesis & delivery April 19.

Team / Mike —

We completed the scheduled runs across US / EU / APAC and the requested failover sweep. High-level results below; attaching raw CSV and a routing summary image. Numbers are median across three runs unless noted.

Summary (chat-heavy profile, model q4_0 except APAC q4_1):
- US (primary): TTFT = 85ms (p50), p95 latency = 170ms, sustained throughput ~ 18k tokens/sec, stable at 320 concurrent sessions before p95 crossed 200ms.
- EU: TTFT = 110ms (p50), p95 = 225ms, throughput ~ 14k tokens/sec, stable at 260 concurrent sessions.
- APAC (q4_1): TTFT = 160ms (p50), p95 = 340ms, throughput ~ 9.5k tokens/sec, stable at 140 concurrent sessions.

Failover/routing sweep: we simulated sudden loss of the primary region and measured cold-routing delta:
- US->EU failover for US clients: median added latency = 85ms (p50), p95 delta = 210ms (observed client-side re-resolve + cold KV warm-up).
- US->APAC fallback (worst case): median added latency = 240ms, p95 delta = 430ms.

Notes & recommendations:
- The APAC region shows clear degradation vs US/EU; using q4_1 reduced memory pressure but increased token latency for TTFT/p95 vs q4_0. We recommend an APAC-specific quant profile plus a warm-KV prefetch strategy for low TTFT.
- For your burst scenario, the US cluster handled 320 concurrent sessions in our test. We observed headroom up to ~360 before tail latencies degraded sharply; we recommend setting production concurrency target to 300 with an autoscale buffer to 380.
- Routing & failover: to reduce cross-region failover deltas, we propose a staged warm-failover where a thin standby KV cache is maintained in the secondary region (adds storage cost but cuts cold-warm delta by ~60%).

Next steps: I’ll compile the measurement table into the MAP summary and flag the action items (config changes, canary plan, SLO wording). Deliverable due April 19.

Attachments: 3-region-stress-results.csv, routing-failover-summary.png
